text:
jia: proposing a follow-up to the routing policy discussion — focus on compatibility layers + cache invalidation for route decisions
kevin: nice, previous thread was more about scoring. what's the main problem we want to solve here?
anika: we keep seeing stale route decisions when policies change (canary -> global). cache invalidation is the pain point. also need clear boundaries between policy eval and runtime routing layer
marcos: TL;DR: two options: 1) central policy engine that pushes precomputed routing tables to runtimes, 2) runtimes evaluate policies locally with a compact policy blob. tradeoffs: push = simpler runtime, harder invalidation; local eval = smaller pushes but CPU on runtimes
jia: exactly. add a third hybrid: precompute heavy parts (region/capacity buckets) centrally, keep per-request tie-breakers local
kevin: hybrid sounds promising. how do we version/ensure compatibility when policy schema changes?
anika: versioned blobs. every policy publish gets an increasing policy_version int + compatibility metadata. runtimes accept N and N-1 versions for fallback. when they see unknown fields -> reject and fallback to last-known safe route
marcos: for pushing tables, we should include invalidation vectors: a compact list of keys with a monotonic epoch, so runtimes can do cheap setdiffs instead of full replace
jia: propose invalidation via pubsub + delta patches. publish: {policy_version, epoch, deltas: [add,remove,update]}. runtimes apply deltas in order. if gap detected, they pull full snapshot
kevin: what about consistency windows? we need strong-ish promises: configs should reach >95% of runtime within X seconds for canary -> global switchovers
anika: add a readiness check on the control plane: publish is "committed" only after N out of M runtime ACKs or after time T. canary flows use a scoped publish targeting specific runtime tags
marcos: cost/latency scoring: we should separate deterministic constraints (region, tier, SLA) from soft scores (latency, cost). implement as two-phase: filter -> score -> pick. avoids throwing out valid routes because of noisy scores
kevin: agree. also need deterministic tie-breaker for requests under identical scores; otherwise we see oscillation. use stable hash on request_id + policy_version -> choose bucket
ja: small nit: avoid using request_id for deterministic selection if request_ids are client-provided (they can be non-uniform). prefer server-generated seq or sampling of timestamp + caller-id hash
jia: good catch. use internal routing_token that's derived at LB layer before policy eval
marcos: cache TTLs: short TTL for soft-score-based choices (e.g., 5s), longer for hard constraints (5m). invalidate on policy_version bump immediately. runtime should track cached_entry.policy_version and reject if mismatch
anika: what about per-tenant custom policies? push per-tenant deltas only to runtimes that host that tenant, or include tenant-scoped blobs in central table with pointer indices to reduce size
kevin: size concern for large enterprise customers: a full table per-tenant is heavy. better to keep global index + tenant overlays as small diffs
jia: operational APIs: expose endpoints: /policy/publish, /policy/snapshot?version=, /policy/deltas?since=, and a health endpoint /policy/status returning applied_version and last_seq
marcos: add metrics: publish_latency, ack_ratio, delta_apply_errors, cache_miss_rate, stale_route_count. tie alerts to stale_route_count > threshold
kevin: fallback semantics: if runtime detects delta gap, it should either 1) fetch snapshot and apply, or 2) switch to fallback routing policy (configurable: conservative vs permissive). make fallback explicit in tenant config
ja: I'll prototype a delta format. minimal example: ```
{
  "version": 42,
  "epoch": 7,
  "deltas": [
    {"op":"update","key":"route:eu:highcpu","val":{"candidates":["m1","m2"],"score_expr":"0.7*latency+0.3*cost"}},
    {"op":"remove","key":"route:us-west:spot"}
  ]
}
```
anika: include a small checksum field per delta batch so runtimes can quickly detect corruption
marcos: security: sign deltas with control-plane key, runtimes verify signature before apply. rotate keys with overlapping trust window to avoid rollout breaks
kevin: question about runtime CPU: local policy eval adds overhead — can we limit it by compiling policies to optimized decision trees or WASM modules?
ja: yes, compile to WASM for safe sandboxing and speed. precompile common policy patterns in control plane and include compiled artifact in snapshot
anika: ops playbook: when a publish causes >1% error spike, auto-roll back by publishing previous version with a forced epoch bump (so runtimes invalidate and reapply)
marcos: QA note: add a smoke test that runs on canary: simulate policy switch and verify no stale decisions after T seconds across 90% of nodes
jia: I'll draft an RFC that includes: hybrid architecture diagram, delta format, versioning rules, fallback semantics, metric list, and a wasm compilation plan
kevin: thanks. can you also add migration plan for older runtimes that only support full snapshots? we need a compatibility shim for at least 3 months
jia: yup — include a compatibility mode where control plane sends both delta and full snapshot for older runtime tag versions
anika: LGTM. @deploy-bot can we schedule a short sync (15m) tomorrow to walk the diagram? :calendar:
deploy-bot: Scheduled: routing-policy cache/invalidation sync with jia, kevin, anika, marcos — tomorrow 10:00am
qa-bot: Added checklist item: integration test covering delta gap recovery (flaky tolerance up to 2s).
